summary: Constantin Sin of the Romanian Ministry of Agriculture said average production of genetically-modified soy rose by 50 tonnes to 250 tonnes per square kilometre last year, and the area cultivated with modified soy increased from 396 km² in 2003 to 581 km² in 2004; GM soy is the only GM crop allowed commercially in Romania and is mainly farmed in southeastern Romania in the counties of Brăila, Călăraşi and Ialomiţa. The European Union endorsed the import of transgenic soy in 1996 and in 2004 approved the sale of new genetically-modified products used for animal breeding, and globally the largest producers of genetically-modified soy are the United States, Argentina and Brazil.
